newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle steady at $64, thin -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle steady at $64, thin -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade on Thursday was slow amid residual sales at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's fairly active movement, feedlot sources said.

About 3,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the weekly movement near 92,000, they said. Kansas sales were close to 1,500 head, with weekly movement about 81,000, the sources said.
The sales at $64.00 also were $2.00 higher than last week's top price. This week's brisk activity kept many feedlots current and sold out most showlists, they said.
Gains this week were powered by strond demand from packers to fill previously booked beef orders, especially among some who were short on nearby cattle supplies, market sources said.
Advances also were attributed to strength in CME live cattle futures and higher trending beef prices, they said.

Beef prices Thursday were quoted up $0.62 to $1.09, with 278 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was at $100.91, up $0.89 from Wednesday and up $1.87 from a week ago, when prices turned higher, the statistics showed.
Outlooks for lighter cattle supplies in the coming weeks and continued declines into the fall, also buoyed prices.
